text:
pagerbot: [ALERT] GPU pool 'g-pool-2' saturation >95% for 3m. Throttled requests increasing. Severity: P1. Autoscales attempted: 2, failed. Reason: scale_limit_hit
mia (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm jumping on it. @jason can you confirm autoscaler logs? any recent rollouts to batching/prefix-cache?
jason (infra): Looking... last deploy 12m ago touched continuous-batching defaults and prefix-cache TTL. Deploy tag: cfg-batch-20260315
jason (infra): tail from autoscaler:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:02Z autoscaler: scale_attempt start, desired=24
2026-03-15T14:02:04Z autoscaler: scale_attempt failed, reason=quota_exceeded pool=g-pool-2 cap=24
2026-03-15T14:05:10Z pods_pending=42 backlog=830 queue_growth=30/s
```
tara (sre): We're seeing queue backlog on g-pool-2 and high prefix-cache miss ratio since that deploy. Metrics:
- prefix_cache_hit_rate: 0.12 (baseline ~0.78)
- avg_batch_window_ms: 1100 (was 350)
- token_throughput_per_gpu: -46% since 14:00
alek (ml-infra): That deploy changed continuous batching to favor larger windows (min_window_ms=800 -> 1200) to optimize cost. Looks like for this workload it increased latency and reduced effective throughput because cache alignment suffered.
mia (oncall): Action plan: 1) temporarily raise pool cap if possible; 2) revert batching window to 350ms; 3) flush prefix cache to repopulate hot keys; 4) notify CS and customers. I'll start 1.
mia (oncall): `kubectl annotate pool g-pool-2 autoscale/override=true --overwrite` then set cap to 40
jason (infra): done, cap bumped to 40. Confirmed with cloud api: capacity now 40. Auto-scaler still showing pending because pods need nodes.
ops-bot: [cloud-provisioner] Requested 4 additional GPU nodes in us-west-2a (ETA ~2m)
alek (ml-infra): Reverting batching config on service 'gen-api' to previous parameters. Applying rollout: `kubectl set configmap gen-api-batching cfg-batch-20260310 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`
jason (infra): Rolling restart on gen-api pods in g-pool-2 to pick up config
```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/gen-api -n prod --selector=pool=g-pool-2
```
customer-support: Noted. We're seeing ~18% of customer requests 5xx/429 during the spike. Opening an incident banner on the status page.
mia (oncall): Flushed prefix cache shard for g-pool-2: `redis-cli -c -h prefix-cache-2 EVAL "return redis.call('FLUSHDB')" 0` (ran on a single shard to avoid global impact)
jason (infra): New nodes came up. Pods scheduled and started. Token throughput recovering.
tara (sre): Cache hit rate improving: 0.54 -> 0.71 over last 4m. Latency SLO for 95th is dropping back toward target.
mia (oncall): Mitigation summary: 1) manual cap bump + nodes provisioned; 2) revert continuous-batching window; 3) flushed prefix cache shard; 4) rolled gen-api pods. Immediate customer impact reduced (~3% errors now).
alek (ml-infra): Root cause hypothesis: recent batching tuning increased batch window for cost reasons, which desynchronized prefix cache access patterns and increased miss storms; autoscaler then hit pool cap under a sudden request surge -> failed to scale in time. Need a fix in the control plane to prevent large batch window increases for latency-sensitive routes.
jason (infra): Filed ticket INFRA-4627 to add autoscale preflight checks and soft-cap autoscaler fallback. Also scheduled a rollback of cfg-batch-20260315 from prod in 30m unless we see regression in metrics.
mia (oncall): Need immediate customer comms: @customer-support please send a short banner: "We experienced elevated errors and throttling for generation workloads in us-west-2. We rolled back a config and capacity is restored. We're investigating root cause and will update in 2h." :loudspeaker:
customer-support: Banner posted. Estimated affected customers: ~6 high-usage tenants; we've opened support tickets with them.
mia (oncall): Post-incident tasks: - add canary for batching config changes - add metric alert for prefix_cache_hit_rate drop - test prefix cache flush playbook - update runbook with explicit steps to raise pool cap safely
tara (sre): I'll own runbook updates. Alek, can your team create a small perf test to validate batch-window vs cache hit tradeoffs?
alek (ml-infra): Yes. Will run a targeted sim tomorrow and send results. Also proposing a safety guard: if prefix_cache_hit_rate < 0.4 then cap batch_window_ms <= 500.
mia (oncall): Closing this thread for live mitigation — monitoring for 30m. If anything spikes, re-alert. Thanks all :heart:
pagerbot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=P1->P2, sla_impact=partial
